angle: Movement translation: per-player similarity between the Combine start-from-stance profile (speed + acceleration every 0.1 s for 1.5 s, matched position drill) and the same player's random NFL snaps; screened over 5 groups x (matched drill, 40); pass rushers chosen as the only group where both curves are reliable enough for a null to be informative (noise ceiling 0.54); held-out test of whether translation explains pressure rate beyond pick.
metric_name: Carry-over: mean absolute gap (sd, after weight and role) between a player's pass-rush-drill curve and his mean random-NFL-rush curve over 0-1.5 s, speed and acceleration; 0 = plays exactly as he tested
headline_number: Carry-over worth -0.27 pressure-rate points per sd on unseen draft classes [-0.67, 0.13], n=68, TOST p=0.001 at +/-1 pt; all 6 Combine-side versions equivalent to zero; drill-to-NFL first-step translation 0.04 [-0.15, 0.22] vs noise ceiling 0.42; same-class pair ranking: pick 61% [52, 70], forecast + Carry-over 61%, + NFL first step 61% (diff vs pick -1 pt [-10, 8]).
what_changed_from_previous: New candidate on the translation angle rather than a revision of round-19 cand_3 (DL 40-start + post-hoc 'Both' rule, 8.07): (1) Combine side is now the matched-stance position drill (pass-rush drill, OL pass-set, WR go route, TE in route, DB backpedal) with the 40 as a second drill, screened across all 5 groups with noise ceilings so the group choice is justified by measurement, not outcome; (2) one nameable metric (Carry-over) with a coach-repeatable definition and the gap drawn in Fig 1; (3) the post-hoc Both rule and 2026 list are dropped; the decision test is a pre-specified pairwise ranking vs pick order with a rusher-clustered interval, honestly tied; (4) baseline includes official 40 and NGS athleticism score; TOST at +/-1 pt for six Combine-side versions; (5) compact ~900-line single-purpose analysis.py, 1,492 words, 4 figures + 1 table, headings carry results, all numbers rendered from numbers.json via template.
open_risks: Pure null paper: the only positive (NFL first step +0.27 pt/sd) does not improve held-out R2 or pair ranking, so the football usability is 'stop doing X' plus a charting protocol.
Pass rushers were chosen after the 10-cell screen; 2 of 10 cells (DL 40, TE 40) clear p<0.05 in-sample, consistent with chance; the DL-40 Carry-over is +0.26 held out.
In-sample Carry-over runs the wrong way (rho -0.21 [-0.38, -0.04]) without a football explanation; held out it is inside the margin.
The +/-1 pt margin is the author's choice (about 3 pressures a season, about the pick-32 vs pick-100 forecast gap); intervals ~+/-0.4 so the verdict depends on it.
NFL curves come from ~19 random sampled rushes per player with no blockers or ball; OL/WR/DB drills have unreliable or single reps, so those groups cannot test translation at all.
